stances_toward.note: Algeria is Spain's largest gas supplier (34.5% of imports in 2025). After the 2022 break (ambassador recalled, 2002 friendship treaty suspended, trade nearly frozen, gas never cut off through Medgaz) came a gradual thaw: Albares in Algiers in Mar 2026, treaty reactivated, Sanchez in Algiers on 20 Jul 2026 with Naturgy, Repsol, Enagas and Moeve and an 8th High-Level Meeting set for October. Warming, but a partner of necessity: Spain has not changed its Sahara position, which is the reason Algeria broke. Bond - none (interest).

stances_toward.note: The crisis opened in 2024 when France endorsed Morocco's autonomy plan and Algeria recalled its ambassador; Boualem Sansal was jailed (5 years, March 2025) and then pardoned on 12 Nov 2025 at the request of Germany's president; France recalled Ambassador Romatet in April 2025 after the expulsion of consular staff; the 1968 migration accord was put under review (Feb 2025). Thaw: Barrot in Algiers 6 Apr 2025, interior minister Nunez in Algiers in Feb 2026, Barrot-Attaf call 15 Mar 2026, journalist Christophe Gleizes still jailed. Rival rather than adversary. Moroccan outlet used for dated facts only. Bond - grievance (colonial).

Warming because the summit was expected to sign more than ten intergovernmental agreements (counter-terrorism to culture); partner, not ally: no alignment treaty. Bond - affinity: the Mattei legacy the two governments invoke.

relations_to.summary: Algeria supplied 34.5% of the natural gas that reached Spain in 2025 (128,504 GWh) and 29.2% in early 2026, mostly through Medgaz; Medgaz flow capacity rose from 28 to 32 million cubic metres a day after the thaw. In May 2022 flows fell by about 25% after the Sahara turn.
relations_to.note: Medgaz capacity figures (28 to 32 mcm/d) come from an Algerian-sourced article; the shares come from the Spanish regulator's numbers as reported by Ara. Sanchez said in Algiers that Algeria is Spain's largest gas supplier this year.
